section: Social stratification and mobility in India
subsections: Middle class and new classes in India
Terms - status inconsistency, status group, life chances

accepted.s: The emergence of the English-educated middle class in India is most directly associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: Macaulay's Minute of 1835 promoted English education, which contributed to the emergence of an English-educated middle class that later participated in the freedom struggle.
accepted.tq: Identify the historical document directly associated with the emergence of the class.
accepted.sec: Middle class and new classes in India

accepted.s:
With reference to the middle class in India, consider the following statements:
1. The World Bank definition mentioned uses a daily per capita income range of 10–50 dollars at purchasing power parity.
2. NCAER placed the annual income range at ₹2–10 lakh at 2001–02 prices.
3. PRICE placed the annual income range at ₹5–30 lakh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly state the income ranges associated with the World Bank, NCAER and PRICE definitions respectively.
accepted.tq: Separate the institutional definitions and check the units, time reference and income ranges.
accepted.sec: Middle class and new classes in India

accepted.s: According to the estimates cited, the Indian middle class comprised approximately what share of the population in 2021?
accepted.x: The middle class was estimated at 43.2 crore, constituting about 31 per cent of India's population in 2021.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the population share from the absolute population figure and other percentages in the subject area.
accepted.sec: Middle class and new classes in India

accepted.s: Which one of the following projections is associated with the future size and global position of India's middle class?
o: It is projected to constitute 67 per cent by 2035 and overtake the United States.
It is projected to constitute 31 per cent by 2047 and overtake China by 2026.
It is projected to constitute 61 per cent by 2047 and may become the world's largest by 2035, overtaking China.
It is projected to constitute 52 per cent by 2035 and remain smaller than China's middle class.
accepted.x: The cited projection places India's middle class at 61 per cent by 2047, while the OECD expects it to become the world's largest by 2035, overtaking China's.
accepted.tq: Match the projection year, percentage and comparative claim without reversing the comparison.
accepted.sec: Middle class and new classes in India

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the occupational base of the Indian middle class?
o: Primarily agricultural labour and subsistence cultivation
Exclusively hereditary occupations and ritual services
Only informal manual work in rural areas
Salaried professionals, white-collar and service jobs, and business
accepted.x: The occupational base includes salaried professionals, white-collar and service-sector workers, and business groups.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that lists the complete occupational cluster rather than an exclusive or narrow description.
accepted.sec: Middle class and new classes in India

accepted.s: The middle class's trust in professional qualifications as a route to mobility was particularly shaken by which event mentioned in the context of 2026?
accepted.x: The 2026 NEET paper leak was cited as an event that shook the middle class's trust in professional qualifications as a pathway to mobility.
accepted.tq: Link the contemporary event to the precise social effect described.
accepted.sec: Middle class and new classes in India

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between education and social mobility in the emerging class system?
o: Education fixes a person's caste position and prevents occupational change.
Education has no relationship with employment or social standing.
Better education generally provides access to better jobs and higher social standing.
Education promotes only horizontal mobility within the same occupation.
accepted.x: Better education is associated with better employment opportunities and higher social standing, thereby enabling upward mobility in the emerging class system.
accepted.tq: Apply the education–employment–status relationship rather than selecting an absolute claim.

accepted.s: The demand for reservation in government jobs by backward classes in South India was prominently associated with which movement?
o: The National Commission for Backward Classes
The Sanskritisation movement of Max Weber
accepted.x: The Self-Respect Movement led by Periyar was associated with demands by backward classes in South India for reservation in government employment.
accepted.tq: Match the social demand with the movement and its leader.

accepted.s: Reservation has contributed to which of the following forms of mobility and social change?
o: Only individual mobility among upper castes
Group mobility and broadening of the urban middle class through the inclusion of backward classes and Dalits
Complete disappearance of caste identity from cities
Restriction of backward classes to traditional occupations
accepted.x: Reservation promoted group mobility and broadened the urban middle class by bringing backward classes and Dalits into new educational and occupational positions.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme claims and identify the option combining the two stated consequences of reservation.

accepted.s: The movement of the Ezhavas of Kerala from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries is an example of:
accepted.x: The shift from toddy tapping to tailoring and cottage industries illustrates occupational mobility among the Ezhavas.
accepted.tq: Use the change in occupation as the decisive clue to the type of mobility.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding migration, urbanisation and caste identity:
1. City anonymity and caste-blind public spaces can weaken caste identity.
2. Migrants may carry caste networks and prejudices into cities.
3. Urbanisation necessarily eliminates caste networks and prejudices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Urbanisation may weaken visible caste identity, but it does not necessarily eliminate caste networks and prejudices; therefore statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Watch for the extreme word 'necessarily' when distinguishing weakening from complete elimination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best identifies Other Backward Classes in the classification described?
o: Communities included in the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes lists
Communities not included in the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes lists
All communities living in rural areas
Only dominant peasant castes seeking political representation
accepted.x: In the classification stated, OBCs are communities that are not included in the SC or ST lists.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the OBC category and the constitutionally listed SC and ST categories.

accepted.s: The Mandal Commission identified OBCs as constituting over what proportion of the population and used how many indicators for their identification?
accepted.x: The Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at over 52 per cent of the population and used 11 indicators: four social, four economic and three educational.
accepted.tq: Pair the population estimate with the total number of indicators, not with unrelated percentages.

accepted.s: The 11 indicators used by the Mandal Commission consisted of:
accepted.x: The indicators comprised four social, four economic and three educational indicators, totalling 11.
accepted.tq: Break the total into its component categories and verify that the sum is 11.

accepted.s:
Dalit social change has taken place through which of the following avenues?
1. State policy
2. Reform movements
3. Sanskritisation and Westernisation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The three avenues identified for Dalit change are state policy, reform movements, and Sanskritisation or Westernisation.
accepted.tq: Check whether the listed avenues are cumulative rather than mutually exclusive.

accepted.s: The demand for OBC status by Marathas, Gujjars and Patels is primarily explained by their pursuit of:
accepted.x: Dominant peasant castes such as Marathas, Gujjars and Patels have demanded OBC status in pursuit of greater life chances.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated motivation behind the demand rather than the identity of the communities.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana caste survey:
1. It ranked 242 castes.
2. It found that 135 castes, constituting 67 per cent of the population, scored above the State average on the backwardness index.
3. It showed that SC/ST households were concentrated mainly in urban areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. SC/ST households remain concentrated in rural areas, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical findings first and reverse the rural–urban location in the false statement.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Concept)
A. Status inconsistency
B. Status group
C. Life chances
D. Closed status group in Weber's analysis

List-II (Associated scholar or description)
1. Gerhard Lenski
2. Max Weber
3. Different rankings across social dimensions
4. Ability to obtain necessities and opportunities for a better life

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Status inconsistency is associated with Gerhard Lenski and means differing rankings across dimensions. Status group and the idea of caste as a closed status group are associated with Max Weber, while life chances refer to access to necessities and opportunities for a better life.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure scholar–concept pairs and then verify the meanings.
accepted.sec: Terms - status inconsistency, status group, life chances

accepted.s: A person who is wealthy but belongs to a low caste, or who is poor but is a Brahmin priest, illustrates:
accepted.x: Status inconsistency occurs when a person occupies different ranks on different dimensions, such as wealth, caste and occupation.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to the contrasting dimensions in the example.
accepted.sec: Terms - status inconsistency, status group, life chances

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Weber's concepts of status group and life chances?
o: A status group is determined only by income, while life chances refer only to ritual purity.
A status group denotes different rankings across dimensions, while life chances mean membership of a closed caste.
A status group shares a lifestyle and social honour, while life chances refer to access to necessities and opportunities shaped by class position and market situation.
A status group is an occupational category, while life chances are fixed exclusively by birth.
accepted.x: Weber described a status group as people sharing a lifestyle and social honour. Life chances concern a person's ability to obtain necessities and opportunities, shaped by class position and market situation.
accepted.tq: Keep the paired definitions separate and reject the swapped meanings of the two terms.
accepted.sec: Terms - status inconsistency, status group, life chances

accepted.s: The reported emergence of a Gen Z horizontal category refers to young Brahmin, Dalit and OBC voters who:
o: Form a category based exclusively on religious identity
Support only their respective traditional caste occupations
Share concerns over jobs and examinations across vertical caste loyalties
Reject all concerns relating to employment and examinations
accepted.x: The horizontal category consists of young voters from different caste groups who share concerns over jobs and examinations, cutting across vertical caste loyalties.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a cross-cutting horizontal concern from a vertically organised caste identity.

accepted.s: According to the Economic Survey estimate cited, poverty declined from 21.9 per cent in 2011–12 to:
accepted.x: The estimate places the decline in poverty from 21.9 per cent in 2011–12 to 2.3 per cent in 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Read the direction of change and match both the base-year and terminal-year values.

accepted.s: Which statement best characterises social stratification and mobility in Kakatiya society?
o: It was stratified but relatively open to mobility, with Velamas, Kammas and Reddys serving in the military and local administration.
It lacked social stratification and had no hereditary groups.
It was entirely closed, and martial castes were excluded from local administration.
It was organised only around urban commercial occupations.
accepted.x: Kakatiya society was stratified but relatively open to mobility. Velamas, Kammas and Reddys formed important elements of the military and local administration.
accepted.tq: Retain both sides of the qualified comparison: stratified, yet relatively open to mobility.

accepted.s: The criticism of Kshatriyaisation in the cases of Marathas, Jats and Yadavs is that it:
o: Brings mobility while reproducing the hierarchy itself
Prevents any form of social mobility and abolishes hierarchy
Concerns only economic migration and not caste status
Creates a casteless social order through reservation
accepted.x: Kshatriyaisation may provide mobility and enhanced status claims, but the criticism is that it reproduces the hierarchical structure rather than eliminating it.
accepted.tq: Recognise the qualified criticism instead of choosing an absolute claim of either mobility or abolition.
